items.name: March in Place
items.description: A gentle way to raise your heart rate and wake up the legs and hips before a workout.
items.setup: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Leave a little space around you.
steps: Lift your right knee toward hip height while swinging your left arm forward.
Lower the right foot softly and lift the left knee, switching arms.
Keep alternating at a steady rhythm, landing quietly on the balls of your feet.
Gradually lift your knees a little higher and swing your arms more as you warm up.
items.breathing: Breathe naturally. You should be able to talk comfortably while marching.
mistakes: Leaning back to lift the knees higher.
Stomping down hard instead of placing the feet softly.
Holding the breath or tensing the shoulders.
items.easier: Keep the knee lift small and hold a wall or chair back for balance.
items.harder: Lift the knees to hip height and pump the arms faster while staying light on your feet.
cautions: Hold onto something stable if your balance is unsteady.

items.name: Arm Circles
items.description: Loosens the shoulders and upper back by moving the arms through gradually larger circles.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Raise your arms out to the sides at shoulder height, palms facing down.
steps: Make small forward circles with straight arms, moving from the shoulders.
Slowly make the circles bigger over the first 10 to 15 seconds.
Halfway through, reverse the direction and circle backward.
Keep your neck relaxed and your ribs down throughout.
items.breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily; avoid holding your breath.
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
Arching the lower back as the arms move.
Moving so fast that the circles become jerky.
items.easier: Keep the circles small, or bend the elbows and circle the fingertips on the shoulders.
cautions: Keep the movement comfortable; reduce the circle size if you feel pinching in the shoulder.

items.name: Shoulder Rolls
items.description: A simple way to release tension in the shoulders and upper back at the start of a workout or during a desk break.
items.setup: Stand or sit tall with your arms relaxed by your sides and your chin level.
steps: Lift both shoulders up toward your ears.
Roll them back and gently squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Lower them down and then forward to complete the circle.
After about half the time, roll in the opposite direction.
items.breathing: Breathe in as the shoulders lift and out as they roll back and down.
mistakes: Rushing through small, tense circles.
Pushing the head forward.
Rolling in only one direction.
items.easier: Do the movement seated and make smaller circles.
cautions: Move within a comfortable range and stop if the movement causes neck pain.

items.name: Standing Hip Circles
items.description: Mobilises the hips and lower back with slow circles, preparing them for squats, lunges and cardio.
items.setup: Stand with your feet a little wider than hip-width, knees soft, and your hands on your hips.
steps: Shift your hips gently to the right, then forward, then left, then back, tracing a circle.
Keep your head and shoulders fairly still while the hips move.
Make the circles slow and smooth, gradually increasing their size.
Switch direction halfway through the set.
items.breathing: Keep breathing easily throughout the movement.
mistakes: Locking the knees.
Moving the whole upper body instead of the hips.
Forcing a range that feels uncomfortable in the lower back.
items.easier: Make smaller circles and hold a chair back for balance.
cautions: Keep the circles small and slow if your lower back is sensitive.

items.name: Standing Torso Rotations
items.description: Gentle standing twists that warm up the spine and the muscles around the waist.
items.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent, and arms bent in front of your chest with elbows out to the sides.
steps: Turn your upper body to the right and let your head follow.
Return through the centre and turn to the left.
Keep your hips facing forward, or let them pivot slightly for a gentler twist.
Use a smooth, controlled rhythm rather than swinging.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you turn and in as you return to the centre.
mistakes: Using momentum to fling the arms around.
Twisting further than is comfortable.
Holding the breath.
items.easier: Reduce the range of the twist and let the hips and heels pivot with you.
cautions: Move gently and within a pain-free range, especially if your back is sensitive.

items.name: Leg Swings
items.description: Dynamic front-to-back swings that loosen the hips and hamstrings before lower-body work.
items.setup: Stand side-on to a wall or sturdy chair and rest one hand on it for balance. Stand on the leg closest to the support.
steps: Lift the outside foot slightly off the floor.
Swing the leg forward in a relaxed arc, then back behind you.
Start with small swings and let them grow as the hip loosens.
Complete the set, then turn around and swing the other leg.
items.breathing: Breathe naturally and keep the swing rhythmic.
mistakes: Kicking up forcefully at the end of the range.
Rounding the back to lift the leg higher.
Locking the knee of the standing leg.
items.easier: Keep the swings small and slow.
items.harder: Swing a little higher while keeping your torso upright and the standing leg steady.
cautions: Keep the swing controlled; it should never feel like a forced stretch.

items.name: Inchworm
items.description: Walk the hands out to a plank and back to warm up the shoulders, core and the backs of the legs.
items.setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, with enough clear floor in front of you for a plank.
steps: Hinge at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees as much as you need.
Walk your hands forward one at a time until you reach a high plank with shoulders over wrists.
Hold the plank briefly with your core braced.
Walk your hands back toward your feet and roll up to standing.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you walk out, keep breathing in the plank, and breathe in as you roll up.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag in the plank.
Walking the hands so far forward that the lower back arches.
Locking the knees while folding forward.
items.easier: Bend the knees generously and walk the hands out only as far as you can control.
items.harder: Add a push-up or one shoulder tap per side once you reach the plank.
cautions: If your wrists are uncomfortable, make fists or place your hands on a raised surface.
Skip this exercise if folding forward causes lower-back pain.
